```{r, include = FALSE}

survey <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(call), ncol = 0))

survey$raceall <- call$Q73
survey$race <- ifelse(survey$raceall == "White", 0, 1)

survey$gender <- NA
survey$gender[call$Q72 == "Woman"] <- 1
survey$gender[call$Q72 == "Man"] <- 0

survey$income <- NA

survey$income[call$Q74 == "Less than $20,000"] <- 1
survey$income[call$Q74 == "$20,000 - $39,999"] <- 2
survey$income[call$Q74 == "$40,000 - $59,999"] <- 3
survey$income[call$Q74 == "$60,000 - $79,999"] <- 4
survey$income[call$Q74 == "$100,000 - $199,999"] <- 5




survey$education <- NA

survey$education[call$Q75 == "Less than high school"] <- 0
survey$education[call$Q75 == "High school diploma or equivalent"] <- 0
survey$education[call$Q75 == "Some college"] <- 0

survey$education[call$Q75 == "2 year degree"] <- 1
survey$education[call$Q75 == "4 year degree"] <- 1

survey$education[call$Q75 == "Master's Degree"] <- 1
survey$education[call$Q75 == "Advanced Degree (PhD, JD, MD, DDS, etc.)"] <- 1



survey$agen <- 2025 - as.numeric(call$Q78)

survey$age[survey$agen >= 17 & survey$agen <= 24] <- "17-24"
survey$age[survey$agen >= 25 & survey$agen <= 34] <- "25-34"
survey$age[survey$agen >= 35 & survey$agen <= 44] <- "35-44"
survey$age[survey$agen >= 45 & survey$agen <= 54] <- "45-54"
survey$age[survey$agen >= 55 & survey$agen <= 64] <- "55-64"
survey$age[survey$agen >= 65 & survey$agen <= 74] <- "65-74"
survey$age[survey$agen >= 75 & survey$agen <= 99] <- "75-99"
survey$age <- factor(
  survey$age,
  levels = c("17-24", "25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-64", "65-74", "75-99")
)

## Self Monitoring

survey$actor <- NA
survey$actor[call$Q47 == "Poor"] <- 0
survey$actor[call$Q47 == "Fair"] <- 0.33
survey$actor[call$Q47 == "Good"] <- 0.66
survey$actor[call$Q47 == "Excellent"] <- 1

survey$impress <- NA
survey$impress[call$ Q45 == "Never"] <- 0
survey$impress[call$ Q45 == "Once in a while"] <- 0.25
survey$impress[call$ Q45 == "Some of the time"] <- 0.5
survey$impress[call$ Q45 == "Most of the time"] <- 0.75
survey$impress[call$ Q45 == "Always"] <- 1


survey$attention <- NA
survey$attention[call$Q46 == "Never"] <- 0
survey$attention[call$Q46 == "Once in a while"] <- 0.25
survey$attention[call$Q46 == "Some of the time"] <- 0.5
survey$attention[call$Q46 == "Most of the time"] <- 0.75
survey$attention[call$Q46 == "Always"] <- 1


survey$self_monitoring <- NA
survey$self_monitoring <- (survey$actor + survey$impress + survey$attention) / 3
## high values = high self montior
mean(survey$self_monitoring, na.rm = TRUE)
#  binary variable
survey$self_monitoring_b <- ifelse(survey$self_monitoring > 0.27, "High Self-Monitor", "Low Self-Monitor")

survey$self_monitoring_quartile <- cut(
  survey$self_monitoring,
  breaks = c(-Inf, 0.1100, 0.2200, 0.4167, Inf),
  labels = c("Very Low", "Low", "High", "Very High"),
  right = TRUE
)
table(survey$self_monitoring_quartile)




survey$PID7 <- NA

# dem
survey$PID7[call$Q4 == "Strong"] <- "Strong Democrat"
survey$PID7[call$Q4 == "Not very strong"] <- "Weak Democrat"

#Experiemental group

survey$PID7[call$Q5 == "Strong"] <- "Strong Democrat"
survey$PID7[call$Q5 == "Not very strong"] <- "Weak Democrat"


survey$PID7[call$Q8 == "Strong"] <- "Strong Republican"
survey$PID7[call$Q8 == "Not very strong"] <- "Weak Republican"

#Experiemental group
survey$PID7[call$Q9 == "Strong"] <- "Strong Republican"
survey$PID7[call$Q9 == "Not very strong"] <- "Weak Republican"



#  Leaners
survey$PID7[call$Q12 == "Democratic"] <- " Leaning Democrat"
survey$PID7[call$Q12 == "Republican"] <- "Leaning Republican"

#Experiemental group
survey$PID7[call$Q13 == "Democratic"] <- " Leaning Democrat"
survey$PID7[call$Q13 == "Republican"] <- "Leaning Republican"



# Pure independents
survey$PID7[call$Q12 == "Neither"] <- "Independent"

#experiemtnal group
survey$PID7[call$Q13 == "Neither"] <- "Independent"


survey$group <- NA

#Control Dem
survey$group[call$Q4 == "Strong"] <- 0
survey$group[call$Q4 == "Not very strong"] <- 0

# Experimental  Dem
survey$group[call$Q5 == "Strong"] <- 1
survey$group[call$Q5 == "Not very strong"] <- 1

#Control  (Rep)
survey$group[call$Q8 == "Strong"] <- 0
survey$group[call$Q8 == "Not very strong"] <- 0

# Experimental  (Rep)
survey$group[call$Q9 == "Strong"] <- 1
survey$group[call$Q9 == "Not very strong"] <- 1

# Control Indep
survey$group[call$Q12 == "Democratic"] <- 0
survey$group[call$Q12 == "Republican"] <- 0

# Experimental Lean
survey$group[call$Q13 == "Democratic"] <- 1
survey$group[call$Q13 == "Republican"] <- 1

# Control pure Ind
survey$group[call$Q12 == "Neither"] <- 0

# Experimental Pure Ind
survey$group[call$Q13 == "Neither"] <- 1

survey$partisan_strength <- NA

# p strength
survey$partisan_strength[survey$PID7 == "Independent"] <- "Independent"
survey$partisan_strength[survey$PID7 == "Leaning Democrat"] <- "Leaning Partisan"
survey$partisan_strength[survey$PID7 == "Leaning Republican"] <- "Leaning Partisan"
survey$partisan_strength[survey$PID7 == "Weak Democrat"] <- "Weak Partisan"
survey$partisan_strength[survey$PID7 == "Weak Republican"] <- "Weak Partisan"
survey$partisan_strength[survey$PID7 == "Strong Democrat"] <- "Strong Partisan"
survey$partisan_strength[survey$PID7 == "Strong Republican"] <- "Strong Partisan"

# ordered factor
survey$partisan_strength <- factor(
  survey$partisan_strength,
  levels = c("Independent", "Leaning Partisan", "Weak Partisan", "Strong Partisan")
)

# Numeric 
survey$partisan_strength_num <- NA
survey$partisan_strength_num[survey$partisan_strength == "Independent"] <- 1
survey$partisan_strength_num[survey$partisan_strength == "Leaning Partisan"] <- 2
survey$partisan_strength_num[survey$partisan_strength == "Weak Partisan"] <- 3
survey$partisan_strength_num[survey$partisan_strength == "Strong Partisan"] <- 4

survey$WMY <- NA
survey$WMY <- paste(
  call$Q10,
```

```{r}
survey <- na.omit(survey)

library('pacman')
pacman::p_load(foreign, ggplot2, dplyr, tidyr, tidyverse, gridExtra,

               stargazer, margins, grid, questionr, rlang, haven, nnet, ggeffects, patchwork, knitr, kableExtra) 

cs3 <- c("#808080", "#FFCCCC", "#FF9999", "#FF6666", "#FF3333", "#CC0000", "#990000")

## Descriptives

ggplot(survey, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +

## PID Strength
ggplot(survey, aes(x = partisan_strength)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "darkred") +

## self monitoring
mean_self_monitoring <- mean(survey$self_monitoring, na.rm = TRUE)
median_self_monitoring <- median(survey$self_monitoring, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(survey, aes(x = self_monitoring)) +
  geom_density(fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_self_monitoring, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median_self_monitoring, color = "blue", linetype = "dotted", size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Density Plot of Self-Monitoring Scores",
       x = "Self-Monitoring Score",
       y = "Density",
       caption = "Red dashed line = Mean | Blue dotted line = Median") +
  theme_minimal()

## Groups

  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
```

```{r}
# Self-Monitoring by Age Group How self-monitoring varies across ages

  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Self-Monitoring Scores by Experimental Group",
```

```{r}
dd <- c("17-24", "25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-64", "65-74", "75-99")
p <- c("Independent", "Weak Partisan", "Leaning Partisan", "Strong Partisan")

study1v2 <- multinom(partisan_strength ~ agen + race + gender + income + education, data = survey)

nomralmodel <- multinom(partisan_strength ~ agen + race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring + group, data = survey)
self_groupmn <- multinom(partisan_strength ~ agen + race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring * group, data = survey)
self_agemn <- multinom(partisan_strength ~  race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring*agen + group, data = survey)
allmn <- multinom(partisan_strength ~ race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring_quartile * group * age, data = survey)
AIC(nomralmodel,self_groupmn,  self_agemn, allmn)



nomralmodelLM <- lm(partisan_strength_num ~ agen + race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring + group, data = survey)
summary(nomralmodelLM)$adj.r.squared

self_ageLM <- lm(partisan_strength_num ~  race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring*agen + group, data = survey)
summary(self_ageLM)$adj.r.squared


self_groupLM <- lm(partisan_strength_num ~ agen + race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring * group, data = survey)
summary(self_groupLM)$adj.r.squared

age_groupm <- lm(partisan_strength_num ~ race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring + group * agen, data = survey)
summary(age_groupm)$adj.r.squared


allLM <- lm(partisan_strength_num ~ race + gender + income + education + self_monitoring * group * agen, data = survey)
summary(allLM)$adj.r.squared



```



```{r}

mn1_pred <- ggpredict(study1v2, terms = c("age"))
mn1_pred$x <- factor(mn1_pred$x, levels = dd)
mn1_pred$response.level <- factor(mn1_pred$response.level, levels= p)
```

```{r}

plot2
```

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1, 4))  
plot(allLM)
# Shapiro-Wilk Test for Normality of residuals
shapiro.test(residuals(allLM))
summary(age_groupm)
tab_model(
  nomralmodelLM,
  self_ageLM,
  self_groupLM,
  age_groupm,
  allLM,        # show standard errors
  digits = 2,             # round to 3 decimal places
  dv.labels = c(
    "Main Effects Only",
    "Self-Monitoring × Age Interaction",
    "Self-Monitoring × Group Interaction",
    "Group × Age Interaction",
    "Self-Monitoring × Group × Age Interaction"
  ),
  pred.labels = c(
    "(Intercept)",
    "Age",
    "Race (0 = White, 1 = Non-White)",
    "Gender (0 = Male, 1 = Female)", 
    "Income",
    "Education",
    "Self-Monitoring",
    "Group (0 = Control, 1 = Experimental)",
    "Self-Monitoring × Age",
    "Self-Monitoring × Group",
    "Group × Age",
    "Self-Monitoring × Group × Age"
  ),
  title = "Regression Models Predicting Partisan Strength"
)

```



```{r}
library(effects)
# Plot the 3-way interaction self_monitoring * group * agen
effect_plot <- Effect(c("self_monitoring", "group"), allLM)

# Plot it
plot(effect_plot,
     multiline = TRUE,          # separate lines for group
     ci.style = "bands",         # confidence intervals as bands
     rug = FALSE,                # no rug plot for data points
     ylab = "Predicted Partisan Strength",
     xlab = "Self-Monitoring",
     main = "Effect of Self-Monitoring, Group, and Age on Partisan Strength")




effect_plot <- Effect(c("self_monitoring", "group"), allmn)

plot(effect_plot,
     multiline = TRUE,
     ci.style = "bands",
     rug = FALSE,
     ylab = "Predicted Probability",
     xlab = "Self-Monitoring",
     main = "Effect of Self-Monitoring and Group on Partisan Strength")
all_effects <- allEffects(allmn)

# Plot all effects
plot(all_effects)

# Correct way
plot(all_effects[["self_monitoring:group:agen"]],
     multiline = TRUE,
     ci.style = "bands",
     rug = FALSE,
     ylab = "Predicted Probability",
     xlab = "Self-Monitoring",
     main = "Interaction: Self-Monitoring × Group × Age")

```





```{r}

kruskal_test_result <- kruskal.test(partisan_strength_num ~ group, data = survey)

kruskal_test_result

pairwise_comparisons <- pairwise.wilcox.test(survey$partisan_strength_num, 
                                              survey$group, 
                                              p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")                                             
                                             
                                             
print(pairwise_comparisons)


# p = 0.428 > 0.05 There is no significant difference in partisan strength distribution between the control and experimental groups.
#Using non-parametric tests, you also find that there is no significant difference in partisan strength between control and experimental groups. The data does not support the idea that the softer question wording changed overall partisan strength scores.


```



```{r}
## does selfmontioring differ across age groups
anova_age_self <- aov(self_monitoring ~ age, data = survey)
summary(anova_age_self)

#anova is singicant p < 0.05 now we need to find out which age group differs, TukeyHSD
TukeyHSD(anova_age_self)


#65-74 group has lower self-monitoring than 25-34 group
# 75-99 group has lower self-monitoring than 25-34 group
# 65-74 group has lower self-monitoring than 35-44 group
# 75-99 group has lower self-monitoring than 35-44 group
#older adults (65-74 and 75-99) have significantly lower self-monitoring compared to young/middle adults (25-44 years old).

```
